SMTO-DB-0017 — The database connection's encryption setting isn't recognized

GUID: f1be8034-62fe-4f2c-b831-21f038be4357
Slug: database-discovery-tls-mode-invalid
Domain: DB · Subsystem: db

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to find the databases on a server, but the setting that controls how the connection is encrypted (sslmode) had a value SMTO doesn't recognize. SMTO didn't connect to anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Set sslmode to one of: disable, allow, prefer, require, verify-ca or verify-full. Check the spelling, including the dash. SMTO only accepts these exact values for the encryption setting.
  2. If you're not sure which value to use, ask the person who manages the database. Servers that use managed security certificates usually expect verify-full. The right value depends on how the server proves who it is, and only its manager knows that.
  3. Send the request again. Nothing was attempted the first time, so it's safe to send again once the setting is valid.

What success looks like

  • The search connects to the server and lists the databases it found as drafts you can review.

If it still fails

  • Ask the person who manages the database which encryption setting to use. Don't switch encryption off just to get past a certificate warning; that can expose your password and data.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A database discovery request's sslmode is not one of disable, allow, prefer, require, verify-ca or verify-full (invalid_sslmode), so no connection was attempted.

What this means

  • A nonempty normalized sslmode is absent from the discovery flow's supported mode set. Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.

Why this can happen

  • A nonempty normalized sslmode is absent from the discovery flow's supported mode set.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact mode with supported choices and the intended server verification requirements.

How to fix it

  • Set sslmode to one of disable, allow, prefer, require, verify-ca or verify-full, or leave it empty to use libpq's default. Choose the mode the server's trust policy requires (verify-full where certificates are managed); do not downgrade to disable or require just to bypass a certificate verification failure.
  • Select a supported sslmode appropriate for the intended server trust requirements. Do not disable verification merely to bypass a certificate failure.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected supported TLS mode retains the intended identity verification.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
